findings.reason: the clause's two live readings differ on options (unbounded domains versus the member's own source domains) for exactly the families the section writes, and the plan's own measure is blind to the difference, so the author must say which rule governs those members before a node writes them.
findings.text: the changed clause says each member of a held-split family "is written the domain decided on its own sources", but the section's own paragraph at plan.html:67 states "The options every family is offered are those of §5, so this section applies §5's decision", and §5's widened options are by definition not bounded by a name's sources; a worker reading "on its own sources" can bound each member's options to its own DD sources, which is the source-bounded rule §2 carried and §5 replaces; the 24 held-split families are the largest families in the catalog (47, 33, 31, 30 members) so this is where the two readings diverge most, and widened-options.json:readings shows the two arms score 0.4864 and 0.4875 on the family member share, so a gate on that share cannot distinguish them

response_events.note: Both sections now say a held-split member is decided as a single name under section 5's options with its own sources as evidence, not bounded to its sources.
